title: Constant-factor entrywise \(\ell_1\) rank-\(k\) approximation with variable \(k\)
formal: Do a uniform randomized polynomial-bit-time algorithm \(A\) and an absolute constant \(C\ge1\) exist such that, for every rational matrix \(M\in\mathbb{Q}^{m\times n}\) and input integer \(0\le k\le\min(m,n)\), \(A\) returns rational factors \(U\in\mathbb{Q}^{m\times k}\), \(V\in\mathbb{Q}^{k\times n}\) satisfying \[\|M-UV\|_1\le C\operatorname{OPT}_k(M),\qquad \operatorname{OPT}_k(M)=\min_{\substack{B\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\\\operatorname{rank}(B)\le k}}\|M-B\|_1,\] with probability at least \(2/3\) on every input?
definitions: \(m,n\ge 1\); dimensions, k and each signed rational numerator and positive denominator are explicitly encoded in binary. The input length L counts the whole dense matrix description. \(\|W\|_1=\sum_{i=1}^{m}\sum_{j=1}^{n}|W_{ij}|\) is the entrywise norm; rank is matrix rank over \(\mathbb{R}\). The optimum is over all real \(m\times n\) matrices of rank at most k and is attained, since a minimizing sequence can be confined to a bounded closed sublevel set. The output consists of binary rational entries of U and V; for \(k=0\) their product denotes the zero matrix. There is a single polynomial P such that A halts within \(P(L)\) Turing-machine steps on every input and every random tape, including the time to write its factors. Therefore the factors have polynomial total encoded length; no unit-cost exact real arithmetic or implicit algebraic-number oracle is available. The approximation factor C and polynomial exponent are independent of m,n,k and entry magnitudes. The probability is over independent fair algorithm coins for each fixed input. Only the displayed multiplicative error is allowed. In particular, when \(\operatorname{rank}(M)\le k\) and \(\operatorname{OPT}_{k}(M)=0\), success requires exact equality \(UV=M\). When the optimum is positive the output need not be an exact real minimizer: the task asks for rational factors meeting the constant-factor inequality. This is the explicit rational bit-model completion of the imported approximation question, not a claim that optimal real factors are rational or efficiently computable.

context_blocks.text: Entrywise absolute error is a standard robust alternative to squared reconstruction error. Exact rank control and a constant independent of k distinguish the target from bicriteria or rank-dependent guarantees.

The existing TCS-7008 asks for a near-optimal relative approximation and does not resolve the weaker but separately significant constant-factor tractability threshold with growing rank. Known fixed-k schemes permit a polynomial exponent depending on k and therefore do not meet this target.

why: Determine whether robust low-rank compression remains computationally tractable with unrestricted target rank.
answer_criterion: Provide a Lean proof that such an algorithm and absolute factor exist with the stated uniform bit bounds, or a Lean proof of their nonexistence. A factor depending on the rank, a polynomial exponent depending on the rank, output rank above the requested rank, or uncharged exact-real computation does not meet this criterion.

sentences: The task compresses a rational matrix while measuring error by the sum of absolute entrywise differences.
The output must have rank at most the supplied rank and approximate the best real matrix of that rank.
Both the approximation factor and polynomial-time exponent must remain independent of the rank.
Known fixed-rank approximation schemes do not meet this joint polynomial-time requirement.
The question asks whether an absolute constant-factor guarantee is possible with explicit rational output.
